title: Streaming teardown coordinator and safer context timeout semantics for Go SDK
creator: Marco Li
description: Background: Several production customers and internal integrations have observed incorrect behavior when client-side context cancellations or tight deadlines race with in-flight streaming responses. Symptoms include: mid-response truncation without explicit error, duplicate resume attempts after partial delivery, KV cache invalidation in downstream runtime, and confusing logs for SLO investigation. Existing tickets address related ergonomics but we need a focused Coordinator abstraction and concrete timeout semantics for the Go SDK streaming surface.
problem_statement: Current Go streaming helper code passes raw context cancellation into lower-level socket and reader loops. This leads to two classes of bugs: (1) aggressive context cancellation causes consumers to miss partial messages and treat the stream as fully failed rather than partially available; (2) ambiguous deadline propagation causes retries to race with server-side commit semantics, occasionally producing duplicate tokens or stale cache artifacts on the runtime side.
proposal:
Implement a 'streaming teardown coordinator' inside the Go SDK that separates connection lifecycle cancellation from per-message/operation deadlines. Key ideas:
- Provide two distinct contexts to users: a connection context (controls transport life) and an optional msgCtx with per-message deadline.
- Normalize deadlines: if msgCtx deadline extends beyond connection context, coordinator will allow message finalization but will close transport only after graceful drain or configured drain timeout.
- Graceful drain: SDK will wait for the current chunk/record boundary (using server-sent EOS/frame marker) up to X ms, then either return a partial response plus a new idempotency token for resume OR surface an explicit truncated error type.
- Retry semantics: retries are only allowed when the coordinator determines the stream was interrupted before server-consensus. We'll add a ResumeToken in the stream metadata when the server supports it.
- Backpressure: keep an internal bounded buffer and expose a default buffer size; when buffer fills, SDK returns ErrBackpressure rather than silently dropping messages.
- Instrumentation: emit metrics for 'drain_wait_ms', 'partial_deliveries', 'resume_attempts', and 'stream_teardown_reasons' and trace spans for 'teardown_coordinator'.
design_notes:
API compatibility: keep StreamReader/StreamWriter API surface minimal. Add optional functional options: WithStreamingCoordinator(WithDrainTimeout(time.Duration), WithBufferSize(int), WithResumeEnabled(bool)) and new error types: ErrStreamTruncated, ErrBackpressure, ErrResumeConflict.
Implementation sketch: coordinator lives in internal/streaming/teardown.go. It orchestrates three goroutines: transport reader, consumer forwarder, and coordinator monitor. Use channels for control signals and atomic boolean for 'finalized'. Avoid context.CancelFunc for cross-goroutine races; instead use explicit close(signal) channels so we can differentiate source-of-close in logs.
Edge cases: server closes immediately after sending a final frame; coordinator should return success. If server never sends EOS and drain timeout elapses, return ErrStreamTruncated with consumed bytes. For resumed streams, ensure ResumeToken is validated server-side; on resume conflict, map to ErrResumeConflict and surface for higher-level retry policy.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes WithStreamingCoordinator options and documented semantics in README
Partial messages are returned with ErrStreamTruncated and include consumed-length metadata
ResumeToken flow validated with integration test against runtime test harness (resume success and conflict cases)
No observable increase in tail latency for normal healthy streams (<= 3% regression in e2e benchmark)
New metrics and trace spans are available in Datadog and linked to existing streaming dashboards
testing_notes: Unit tests for coordinator goroutine cancellation ordering (simulate cancellation from consumer, simulate transport error, simulate server EOS)
Fuzz tests for boundary conditions: partial frame boundaries, mid-frame cancellations, large messages > buffer size
Integration test against runtime-integration harness that can inject 'pause before EOS' and return a resume token
Performance benchmark: run existing streaming latency/cost harness with and without coordinator enabled; target <= 3% overhead in P95 latency for 1k concurrent streams
tasks: Write teardown coordinator implementation in internal/streaming
Add options and types to public package for opt-in behavior
Create unit + integration tests and CI job targeting integration harness
Add metrics/traces and hook into console dashboards
Update Go SDK README and migration notes
Open PR and request review from runtime and SDK owners
rollout_plan: Feature behind opt-in flag defaulting to disabled for 2 minor releases
Alpha rollout to internal baking org and two pilot customers using dedicated capacity
Monitor metrics for 'partial_deliveries' and 'resume_attempts' for 2 weeks
Graduate to default-on in sdk-go-0.13 after no major regressions
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: introducing buffer adds memory pressure for bursty clients. Mitigation: configurable buffer size and default small footprint (8 messages).
Risk: resume flow complexity might surface runtime bugs. Mitigation: gated integration tests and a decay policy to disable resume for early adopters.
Risk: confusing error types for users. Mitigation: document clear examples and translation helpers that map truncated errors to structured results for common patterns.
